extraFacts.fact: Indus listings in the same range: nuclear ball and butterfly valves are published to DN1500 (ball) and DN3000 (butterfly); nuclear gate, globe and check valves up to DN600; power plant butterfly and ball valves cover butterfly 2" to 72" and ball 1/2" to 24"; power plant high-pressure gate valves DN50 to DN750 in ASME Class 900 to 4500, globe DN15 to DN50, check DN50 to DN800 in Class 150 to 2500.
extraFacts.source: Indus Hydraulics listings for the four power and nuclear valve ranges

faqs.q: What are nuclear ball and butterfly valves, Safety Class 1, 2 and 3, used for?
faqs.a: They are quarter-turn isolation valves for nuclear cooling water, ventilation, containment and auxiliary systems. Ball valves isolate lines up to DN1500 with soft or metal seals, and butterfly valves handle the largest cooling-water and ventilation lines up to DN3000. Designs are qualified by life-cycle and seismic testing.

faqs.q: What sizes do nuclear ball and butterfly valves cover?
faqs.a: Ball valves are published up to DN1500 and butterfly valves up to DN3000. Ends can be wafer, lug, raised-face flanged, butt-weld, socket weld or NPT, and drives are manual, pneumatic, electric or remote. Dimensions depend on size, rating and options, and the general arrangement drawing comes with the quotation.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature can nuclear ball and butterfly valves handle?
faqs.a: Design pressure is up to 25 MPa, with temperatures up to 370 °C for ball valves and 450 °C for butterfly valves. The actual rating of a valve depends on size, body material and seat, so quote the design pressure and temperature and we confirm the build.

faqs.q: What body materials are offered on nuclear ball and butterfly valves?
faqs.a: Bodies are available in stainless steel, carbon steel and alloy steel, with soft or metal seats on ball valves. The choice depends on the medium, the temperature and the safety class of the system. Tell us the fluid and design conditions and we will confirm material and seat.

faqs.q: What do Safety Class 1, 2 and 3 mean for nuclear ball and butterfly valves?
faqs.a: The class reflects how critical the system is: Class 1 covers the reactor coolant pressure boundary, and Classes 2 and 3 cover progressively less critical safety systems. The class sets materials, examination and documentation. Design references are the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and seismic category I.

faqs.q: Which end connections and drives do nuclear ball and butterfly valves offer?
faqs.a: Ends are wafer, lug, raised-face flanged, butt-weld, socket weld or NPT. Drives are manual, pneumatic, electric or remote. State the line connection and the operator torque or air supply when you enquire. For the non-return or isolation duty on the same system see the [nuclear gate, globe and check valves](/p/nuclear-gate-globe-check-valves).

faqs.q: What tests apply to nuclear ball and butterfly valves before delivery?
faqs.a: Valves get shell and seat tests to ASME B16.34 and API 598, with the qualification tests the project specifies, and the pressure-test record is supplied with the valve. Third-party inspection and extra tests are added when the order specifies them.

faqs.q: Where are large nuclear butterfly valves used?
faqs.a: They are used on essential service water, component cooling water and containment ventilation, where very large bores must isolate reliably. Butterfly valves cover the largest lines, up to DN3000, while ball valves handle isolation up to DN1500.

faqs.q: How do nuclear ball and butterfly valves differ from the power plant butterfly and ball valves?
faqs.a: The nuclear valves carry safety classification, seismic qualification and a documented quality programme, with ball valves to DN1500 and butterfly valves to DN3000. The [power plant butterfly and ball valves](/p/power-plant-butterfly-and-ball-valves) cover balance-of-plant duty, with butterfly valves 2" to 72" and ball valves 1/2" to 24".

faqs.q: What documents come with nuclear ball and butterfly valves?
faqs.a: Each valve comes with material certificates to EN 10204 3.1, the pressure-test record and the general arrangement drawing. The ball and butterfly general arrangement drawing shows face-to-face length and operator mounting. Third-party inspection and extra tests can be added when the order specifies them.

faqs.q: How are nuclear ball and butterfly valves supplied and how long do they take?
faqs.a: The nuclear ball and butterfly valves are supplied from Dubai to projects and plants across the GCC, the wider Middle East and Africa. Most are built to the order specification, so delivery depends on size, class, material and operator; standard carbon-steel sizes move fastest. Data sheets and drawings are issued with the quotation.

faqs.q: What do I send to get a quotation for nuclear ball and butterfly valves?
faqs.a: Send the valve data sheet if you have one; otherwise the size, pressure class, body and trim material, end connection with the pipe schedule, operator, design temperature and service fluid. Add the safety class, seismic category and any qualification the project requires. Use [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What are nuclear gate, globe and check valves, Safety Class 1, 2 and 3, used for?
faqs.a: They are isolation and non-return valves for the primary, secondary and auxiliary systems of nuclear plants. Gate valves isolate, globe valves throttle and check valves stop backflow. Each design is qualified by a life-cycle programme and built under a nuclear quality programme.

faqs.q: What sizes and pressures do nuclear gate, globe and check valves cover?
faqs.a: The published range is up to DN600, with design pressure up to 25 MPa. End connections are butt-weld, raised-face flanged, socket weld or NPT. These valves are engineered per system and class, so data sheets and drawings are issued with the quotation.

faqs.q: What temperature can nuclear gate, globe and check valves handle?
faqs.a: The published figure is up to 370 °C, with design pressure up to 25 MPa. The rating of a particular valve depends on its size, body material and class, so state the design pressure and temperature on the data sheet and we confirm the build.

faqs.q: What body materials are offered on nuclear gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: Bodies are stainless steel, carbon steel or alloy steel. The material follows the safety class, the temperature and the medium in the system. Send the fluid and design conditions and we will confirm the grade before quoting.

faqs.q: What do the safety classes mean for nuclear gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: Class 1 covers the reactor coolant pressure boundary, and Classes 2 and 3 cover progressively less critical safety systems. The class sets materials, examination and documentation. Designs refer to the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and seismic category I.

faqs.q: Which ends and operators fit nuclear gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: Ends are butt-weld, raised-face flanged, socket weld or NPT, and operation is manual, pneumatic, electric or remote. Quarter-turn isolation on the same system comes from the [nuclear ball and butterfly valves](/p/nuclear-ball-butterfly-valves). Give the pipe schedule for butt-weld ends.

faqs.q: How are nuclear gate, globe and check valves qualified and tested?
faqs.a: Each design is qualified by a life-cycle programme that includes 2,000 cycles at temperature, flow interruption and seismic testing. Production valves get shell, seat and backseat tests to ASME B16.34 and API 598, with the pressure-test record supplied.

faqs.q: Which nuclear systems use gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: They serve the primary, secondary and auxiliary systems of nuclear plants. Gate valves provide isolation, globe valves regulate or isolate small lines, and check valves protect equipment from reverse flow.

faqs.q: How do nuclear gate, globe and check valves differ from the power plant high-pressure gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: The nuclear valves reach DN600 and carry safety classification and seismic qualification, with design pressure up to 25 MPa. The [power plant high-pressure gate, globe and extraction check valves](/p/power-plant-high-pressure-gate-globe-check-valves) are for steam and feedwater duty in ASME Class 900 to 4500, with gate valves up to DN750.

faqs.q: What documents come with nuclear gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: Each valve comes with material certificates to EN 10204 3.1, the pressure-test record and the general arrangement drawing. Because the safety class sets the examination and documentation, state the class in the enquiry. Third-party inspection and extra tests can be added when the order specifies them.

faqs.q: How are nuclear gate, globe and check valves supplied and how long do they take?
faqs.a: The nuclear gate, globe and check valves are supplied from Dubai to projects and plants across the GCC, the wider Middle East and Africa. Most are built to the order specification, so delivery depends on size, class, material and operator; standard carbon-steel sizes move fastest. Data sheets and drawings are issued with the quotation.

faqs.q: What do I send to get a quotation for nuclear gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: Send the valve data sheet if you have one; otherwise the size, pressure class, body and trim material, end connection with the pipe schedule, operator, design temperature and service fluid. Add the safety class, pattern (gate, globe or check) and the qualification the project requires. Use [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What are power plant butterfly and ball valves used for?
faqs.a: They are quarter-turn valves for the balance of plant: circulating and cooling water, condensate, compressed air, drains and hydro-electric stations. Butterfly valves give tight shut-off in concentric, double or triple offset designs, and ball valves cover small-bore and high-pressure isolation.

faqs.q: What sizes and pressure classes do power plant butterfly and ball valves cover?
faqs.a: Butterfly valves run from 2" to 72" and ball valves from 1/2" to 24". Pressure classes are ASME Class 150 to 2500, and ball valves go up to Class 4500. The general arrangement drawing with each quotation gives the dimensions.

faqs.q: What pressure classes are available on power plant butterfly and ball valves?
faqs.a: Classes run from ASME Class 150 to 2500, and ball valves extend to Class 4500. Butterfly valves are used in the lower classes for water and air, and trunnion ball valves take the high-pressure isolation duty. We confirm the class from your data sheet.

faqs.q: What materials are power plant butterfly and ball valves made from?
faqs.a: Bodies are cast iron, carbon steel, stainless steel or alloy steel, with corrosion-resistant alloy options for seawater cooling. The choice follows the medium and temperature. Tell us whether the line carries fresh water, seawater, condensate or air and we will confirm the build.

faqs.q: Which standards cover power plant butterfly and ball valves?
faqs.a: The design standards are API 609 for butterfly valves and ASME B16.34 for pressure-temperature ratings. Valves get shell and seat tests to ASME B16.34 and API 598, with any further qualification tests your project specifies.

faqs.q: What end connections and operators suit power plant butterfly and ball valves?
faqs.a: Butterfly valves are wafer, lug or flanged, and ball valves are butt-weld, socket weld or raised-face flanged. Operation is by handwheel, gearbox, pneumatic, hydraulic or electric actuator. For steam and feedwater isolation see the [power plant high-pressure gate, globe and check valves](/p/power-plant-high-pressure-gate-globe-check-valves).

faqs.q: How should a power plant butterfly or ball valve be specified for an actuator?
faqs.a: State the operator type, the differential pressure and the required closing time, because actuator torque must be sized for the valve and not assumed. We flag an unsized operator torque before quoting. Handwheel, gearbox, pneumatic, hydraulic and electric operation are all offered.

faqs.q: Where are power plant butterfly and ball valves used?
faqs.a: They are used on circulating and cooling water, condensate, compressed air and drains, and in hydro-electric stations. Butterfly valves suit the large cooling-water lines, and ball valves suit small-bore and high-pressure isolation.

faqs.q: How do power plant butterfly and ball valves differ from nuclear ball and butterfly valves?
faqs.a: Power plant valves are for balance-of-plant duty, while the [nuclear ball and butterfly valves](/p/nuclear-ball-butterfly-valves) add safety classification, seismic qualification and a documented quality programme. Nuclear butterfly valves are published to DN3000, against 72" for the power plant range.

faqs.q: What documents come with power plant butterfly and ball valves?
faqs.a: Each valve comes with material certificates to EN 10204 3.1, the pressure-test record and the general arrangement drawing. Where the line carries seawater, the certificates cover the disc and shaft alloys chosen for it. Third-party inspection and extra tests can be added when the order specifies them.

faqs.q: How are power plant butterfly and ball valves supplied and how long do they take?
faqs.a: The power plant butterfly and ball valves are supplied from Dubai to projects and plants across the GCC, the wider Middle East and Africa. Most are built to the order specification, so delivery depends on size, class, material and operator; standard carbon-steel sizes move fastest. Data sheets and drawings are issued with the quotation.

faqs.q: What do I send to get a quotation for power plant butterfly and ball valves?
faqs.a: Send the valve data sheet if you have one; otherwise the size, pressure class, body and trim material, end connection with the pipe schedule, operator, design temperature and service fluid. Add the offset design, seat type and whether the line carries seawater. Use [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What are power plant high-pressure gate, globe and extraction check valves used for?
faqs.a: They are for main steam, reheat, feedwater, extraction and drain systems in supercritical and ultra-supercritical plants. Gate valves isolate, small-bore bonnetless globe valves serve drains and vents, and swing extraction check valves close with power assistance.

faqs.q: What sizes do power plant high-pressure gate, globe and check valves cover?
faqs.a: Gate valves run from DN50 to DN750, globe valves from DN15 to DN50 and check valves from DN50 to DN800. Ends are butt-weld, with socket weld or threaded ends on small bores. The general arrangement drawing comes with the quotation.

faqs.q: What pressure classes do power plant gate, globe and extraction check valves cover?
faqs.a: Gate and globe valves are ASME Class 900 to 4500, and check valves are Class 150 to 2500. Power-station valves work at supercritical pressures, temperatures above 500 °C and constant cycling, so confirm the design pressure and temperature when you enquire.

faqs.q: Which alloy steels are used for high-temperature power plant valves?
faqs.a: The range uses high-temperature alloy steels WC9, C12A, F91 and F92, as well as carbon steel and stainless steel bodies. The grade follows the steam temperature and pressure of the line. State the design conditions and we will confirm the material.

faqs.q: Which standard governs power plant high-pressure gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: The design standard is ASME B16.34. Valves get shell, seat and backseat tests to ASME B16.34 and API 598, with the qualification tests the project specifies, and the pressure-test record comes with the valve.

faqs.q: What end connections and operators suit power plant high-pressure gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: Ends are butt-weld, with socket weld or threaded ends on small bores. Operation is by handwheel, gearbox, pneumatic, hydraulic or electric actuator. For cooling-water isolation see the [power plant butterfly and ball valves](/p/power-plant-butterfly-and-ball-valves).

faqs.q: Why are power-assisted extraction check valves used?
faqs.a: On a turbine trip, steam in the extraction lines can flow back into the turbine and overspeed it. A power-assisted check valve closes fast to prevent that. The swing disc closing assist can be pneumatic, hydraulic or electric.

faqs.q: Which systems use power plant gate, globe and extraction check valves?
faqs.a: They are used on main steam, reheat, feedwater, extraction and drain systems in supercritical and ultra-supercritical plants. Small-bore bonnetless globe valves serve drains and vents.

faqs.q: How do power plant high-pressure valves differ from the nuclear gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: The power plant valves are ASME Class 900 to 4500 with gate valves to DN750 for steam and feedwater duty. The [nuclear gate, globe and check valves](/p/nuclear-gate-globe-check-valves) reach DN600 and add safety classification, seismic qualification and life-cycle qualification.

faqs.q: What documents come with power plant high-pressure gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: Each valve comes with material certificates to EN 10204 3.1, the pressure-test record and the general arrangement drawing. For alloy grades such as F91 or F92 the certificates record the grade supplied. Third-party inspection and extra tests can be added when the order specifies them.

faqs.q: How are power plant high-pressure valves supplied and how long do they take?
faqs.a: The power plant high-pressure valves are supplied from Dubai to projects and plants across the GCC, the wider Middle East and Africa. Most are built to the order specification, so delivery depends on size, class, material and operator; standard carbon-steel sizes move fastest. Data sheets and drawings are issued with the quotation.

faqs.q: What do I send to get a quotation for power plant high-pressure gate, globe and check valves?
faqs.a: Send the valve data sheet if you have one; otherwise the size, pressure class, body and trim material, end connection with the pipe schedule, operator, design temperature and service fluid. Add the steam or feedwater conditions and the body alloy grade you need. Use [our contact page](/contact).
